intro.en: Cuando plus the subjunctive looks forward. Cuando plus the indicative is a habit.

llegue.consejo: Before e, g sounds like j.

bloques.texto:
A habit that already happens uses the ordinary present.

- **Cuando tengo** tiempo, leo.

Something that has **not happened yet** uses the subjunctive.

- **Cuando tenga** tiempo, te llamaré.
- **En cuanto llegue**, te escribo.

The future idea can sit in the other half of the sentence (llamaré) or just in the meaning.

frases.en: When I have time, I read.
When I have time, I'll call you.
As soon as I arrive, I'll write to you.

pregunta.en: The call has not happened yet. Which one?

Cuando tenga tiempo, te llamaré.en: Not yet: subjunctive in the cuando clause.

Cuando tengo tiempo, leo.en: That is a habit. It already happens.

Ayer te llamé.en: That is finished. It is the indefinido.

tenga.en: The time is still in the future, so the subjunctive.

pregunta.en: Complete: call me when you arrive.

llegues.en: It has not happened yet: subjunctive.

pregunta.en: Complete the habit: when I have time, I read.

tenga.en: Tenga would look at the future.

traduccion.en: As soon as I arrive, I'll write to you.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write what you will do when certain things happen: when you finish your studies, retire, have money, speak Spanish well.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain your plans aloud step by step: En cuanto…, cuando…, después de que…
